end.parentNote: Jiya practised checking whether a number can be split into complete pairs, using counters and examples such as 6, 7, and 47. They explained the pairing for 6 and 7, and later corrected the mix-up about 47 by finding 23 pairs with 1 left; the digit-by-digit confusion was not fully settled by the end. At home, practise with small groups of buttons or coins and ask, “Can they all be put into pairs, or is one left?”
